chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said: Bashir ibn Yasar narrated to me, saying:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in fanak fur, fira', squirrel fur, sable, and hawasil that are hunted in the lands of shirk or in the lands of Islam: may I perform salat (prayer) in it without taqiyyah? He said: So he said: Perform salat (prayer) in squirrel fur and the Khwarazmian hawasil, and do not perform salat (prayer) in foxes nor in sable.

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes, whose fur is ruled impermissible for salat (prayer)
key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sable, identified here as impermissible for salat (prayer)
key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: squirrel fur, identified here as permissible for salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْحَوَاصِلِ: hawasil, a type of fur or hide referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْفَنَكِ: fanak fur, a type of animal fur mentioned in the legal query
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: taqiyyah, precautionary dissimulation; here indicating the question concerns praying without such precaution

ai.seo_question: Which animal furs are permissible or impermissible to wear during salat (prayer) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling concerning the permissibility of performing salat (prayer) in garments made from certain animal furs. It distinguishes between types of fur, permitting salat (prayer) in squirrel fur and Khwarazmian hawasil, while prohibiting it in fox and sable.
